Subject: Re: Invoice & VAT approach for multi-entity pilot (Greenline)

Hi Amal — thanks for the clear note and the PO. We can support both approaches; recommended options are below with trade-offs so you can pick what maps best to your AP processes.

Option 1 — Consolidated invoice (single invoice to Greenline):
- Redwood issues one invoice to Greenline with line items tagged by cost center / legal entity (e.g., "US Entity - 100 seats", "IE Entity - 50 seats").
- We include per-line tax treatment and a remit block for each legal entity that needs to be paid separately (bank details, entity name, VAT ID).
- Pros: single invoice file for your AP; consistent payment timing.
- Cons: your AR system must apply lines to different GL accounts / cost centers at posting.

Option 2 — Per-entity invoices (separate invoices for US and IE):
- Two invoices issued, each with only the lines for that legal entity.
- Pros: cleaner posting per entity; simpler VAT handling per invoice.
- Cons: multiple payments and potentially multiple POs needed on your side.

For the pilot, many customers choose option 1 to keep procurement simple; we provide a machine-readable CSV + PDF with per-line entity tags so your AP can auto-allocate during EDI or manual posting.

Next steps / info we need from you:
- Confirm whether you prefer consolidated invoice or per-entity invoices.
- If consolidated: supply the legal entity mapping (PO -> legal entity) and VAT numbers for entities that will be paying. I attached an entity mapping template we use.
- If per-entity: confirm separate PO numbers for each legal entity.

I attached the entity_mapping_template.xlsx for your finance team to fill out — once we have that we will produce a sample invoice and remit instructions for signoff. If helpful, we can also loop in our tax vendor (ZenLedger) to confirm EU reverse charge language.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Vivek — quick notes from ops / accounting perspective:

- If we do consolidated invoice we must ensure each remit block has a clear pay-to legal entity and bank details; also each line must include an internal ledger tag so our billing system can emit an "allocation statement" tied to the consolidated invoice (this is how customer AP posts correctly).
- For EU (Ireland) seats: likely reverse charge applies if Greenline is VAT-registered; need their VAT ID and a written confirmation that the service is used for business purposes. Without that we may be obligated to charge VAT (unlikely but need to check).
- Request: Marissa, can you prepare a Per-Entity ledger mapping and confirm whether we can emit a CSV that contains the GL account and cost center columns? That will be attached to the invoice as 'Allocation CSV'.
- Ben: when we issue a consolidated invoice we should include an "Entity Allocation Statement" PDF and a single-page remit summary for AP. This reduces back-and-forth.

I can pre-check the SOW to see if an amendment is required to list billing/legal entities as parties. If so, we'll push a short DocuSign amendment.

Subject: Re: Quick VAT confirmation — Greenline Health (pilot)

Vivek / Kimberly — short checklist attached below. High level: consolidated invoice with per-line reverse-charge notation is acceptable for VAT recovery PROVIDED you include the following for the IE lines:
- Customer VAT number (validate format: IE*********)
- Supplier VAT number (Redwood EU entity VAT id)
- Clear statement: "Reverse charge — Article 194/196" or local phrasing if requested
- Line-level service description, net amounts, and VAT amount (zero where reverse-charge applied)
- Allocation CSV containing invoice line id, legal_entity, cost_center, customer_vat, supplier_vat

We also recommend a simple attestation e-mail from the customer confirming they are VAT-registered in the IE jurisdiction for the services covered (can be included as part of the PO).

Link: https://zenledger.example.com/checklists/eu-reverse-charge

—ZenLedger Tax Ops
Attachment: eu_reverse_charge_checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

Subject: Final: invoicing approach & next steps for pilot

Hi Amal — following internal and tax review, here's the approach we recommend for the pilot and the items we need from your team to proceed.

Chosen approach: Consolidated invoice with per-line entity allocation and separate remit blocks. This minimizes the number of invoice files while giving your AP the per-entity detail needed to post correctly.

We will provide on invoice delivery:
- PDF invoice (single file) with line items labeled by legal entity and net amounts.
- Allocation CSV with columns: invoice_line_id, legal_entity_name, legal_entity_vat, cost_center_code, net_amount.
- Entity Allocation Statement PDF that summarizes totals per legal entity and explicit remit instructions (bank details per entity).

What we need from Greenline:
1) Confirm you accept a consolidated invoice with allocation CSV (yes/no).
2) Complete the attached entity_mapping_template.xlsx with: legal_entity_name, legal_entity_vat, PO_number (if per-entity POs exist), and cost_center_code.
3) If any IE lines should use reverse charge, please provide the Irish VAT number(s) and a short confirmation in reply to this thread.

Timing: once we receive the completed mapping we will send a sample invoice and allocation CSV within 48 business hours. If any contractual amendment is needed to reflect multiple pay-tos in the SOW, we will send a one-page DocuSign amendment (link included).

DocuSign link: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/GLH-amend-2026

Attachments: entity_mapping_template.xlsx, Greenline_SOW_v2.docx

Let me know if you'd prefer separate invoices instead and we'll route that flow.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this set up.
